messages:
lena: Heads-up — we're seeing a p99 jump on /v1/generate across a subset of Dedicated GPU hosts after last night's CUDA+driver rollout. p95 up ~3x, p99 up ~9x. A couple of customers filed escalations.

samir: Oof. Which fleet/AMI/driver version? Any correlation with instance types or NVMe models?

lena: Rolling out CUDA 13.1 + nvidia-driver 540.XX to the dedicated pool (fleet-dedicated-eu-west). Affected hosts look to be those with PM1725 NVMe and kernel 6.4.

maya: Adding short traces from one host. Notice tail latency clusters around NVMe IO wait.

maya: ```
# top: threads waiting on io
PID USER PR NI VIRT RES SHR S %CPU %MEM TIME+ COMMAND
2345 red  20 0  1.2g  500m  10m S  5.0  1.1 0:12.34 python -u server
...
# iostat -x 1 3
Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s rsec/s wsec/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util
nvme0n1 0.00 0.00  12.00  32.00  640.00  4096.00 64.00  2.50  15.00 12.00 16.00 0.50 1.80

# dmesg snippets
[ 1234.567890] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456
[ 1234.568000] nvme nvme0: controller error status: 0x12
```

ben: Those nvme errors are worrying. Are we seeing firmware mismatches? Also, did the driver change any default qdisc or IO scheduler behavior?

samir: Good call. CUDA/driver upgrades sometimes pull in kernel modules with different submission patterns. We should verify kernel parameters, qdisc, and NVMe queue depth.

lena: I already rolled collected histograms for p99 by host and correlated them with kernel versions. Hosts on 6.4 with pm1725 show the worst numbers; older kernel 5.15 hosts are fine.

oncall-ops: Deploy-bot triggered a canary group rollback? Not yet. We want mitigations first that don't require full rollback.

ops-bot: @deploy-bot requested to start targeted routing to healthy hosts.

samir: Quick mitigations to try (low-risk):
- Drain affected hosts from traffic routing (shift to older pool).
- Set NVME IO scheduler to 'none' and disable multiqueue qdisc (if we suspect qdisc-induced latencies).
- Increase nvme queue_depth to 1024 at kernel module params.
- Temporarily pin CUDA kernels to older driver using module blacklist if feasible.

maya: I can push a qdisc change and bump queue_depth on one problematic host to validate. Command I'm planning: 
```bash
# set no qdisc offload
netethool -K eth0 tx-offload off rx-offload off
# change IO scheduler
echo none > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/scheduler
# bump queue depth (example for pm1725)
echo 1024 > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/nr_requests || true
# reload nvme module (careful)
modprobe -r nvme && modprobe nvme
```

ben: Careful with modprobe -r on production. Better to test on a drained host first. Also capture perf and iostat before/after.

lena: Doing action: draining host i-0a1b2c3d (canary). Removing from LB; cordoning tasks. Will then run Maya's changes.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback triggered for host group cg-rt-12 (started 2862001300). Rolling routing over 5min.

maya: Ran the IO scheduler change on i-0a1b2c3d and bumped nr_requests. Early numbers: p99 for that host fell from ~2.3s to ~420ms for a 10-minute window. iostat shows avgqu-sz dropped from 3.2 to 0.6.

samir: That's promising — points to NVMe queueing interacting poorly with driver. Any kernel oops in dmesg after change?

maya: No new errors after change. Old dmesg errors predate the mitigations.

lena: Routing now shifted off affected pool to older-kernel pool — customer-facing p99 dropped cluster-wide in the last 12 minutes. Escalations queued for update.

ben: Longer-term: need a triage plan with infra/release. Options: revert driver rollout, coordinate with NVMe firmware vendor for pm1725, or test kernel 6.4 with NVMe firmware microcode update. Also add an automated regression check for IO tail latency in canary matrix.

samir: Agreed. Assignments:
- maya: run a controlled test matrix (kernel 6.4 + driver 540 + pm1725) in lab and attempt to reproduce exact avgrq-sz/await pattern. Due EOD.
- lena: communicate to Support/Customer Success with mitigation summary and ETA for a permanent fix.
- ben: open ticket with NVMe vendor + nvidia driver team; include dmesg and iostat samples.
- oncall-ops: keep the routing shift until we have a validated driver/kernel combo.

oncall-ops: Noted — keeping shifted routing and watching for regressions. Will re-open traffic gradually once lab results look good.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback completed at 2862001350. Routing moved to healthy pool.

lena: Closing loop with support: we've mitigated customer impact by routing away from affected hosts and applying per-host qdisc/queue tuning as an emergency measure. We're investigating root cause (likely driver<->nvme queue interactions on kernel 6.4 + pm1725). Will provide regular updates.

samir: One follow-up: add a smoke test that runs a short NVMe IO pattern on any host that receives new driver/firmware during rollout, verifying avgq and await thresholds before flipping full traffic.

maya: On it — will prototype a canary probe and post results.

lena: Thanks everyone. If nothing else shows up we'll keep this thread for final RCA and postmortem notes.

ops-bot: Incident annotated: type=latency, impact=customer_escalations, mitigation=targeted-routing+io-tune, status=monitoring
